summary:
Farmanac is a farmer’s almanac rewritten with NASA data. We built a simple web tool that helps farmers compare crop rotations while the climate is changing.

The farmer picks a field on a satellite map or types coordinates. Farmanac loads ten years of daily NASA POWER data for that spot (rainfall, temperature, frost days and very hot days). The farmer says what matters most: saving water, income or soil health. Farmanac then ranks rotations built from the crops common in the region, or from crops the farmer chooses. Each option explains why it is suggested, its benefits, the risks to check with a local expert and what the tool does not know. A “bad year” test also scores every rotation for the driest and the hottest year, showing which options hold up under stress.

This matters because shifting weather, water shortages and tired soil make rotation choices harder. Farmanac supports farmers’ judgment and local expertise instead of replacing them.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

Farmanac helps a farmer compare crop rotations using NASA data. The farmer picks a field on a satellite map or types coordinates. The page then asks the NASA POWER API for ten years of daily data for that point (rainfall and minimum, mean and maximum air temperature) and turns it into simple numbers: yearly rain, average temperature, frost days and very hot days, plus a monthly chart. The farmer sets what matters (saving water, income, soil health) and picks the rotation they use now. Farmanac builds rotation options from the crops common in the region, or from crops the farmer chooses, and ranks them. Crops of the same plant family are not placed next to each other, and mixing families earns a small bonus because it helps break pest and disease cycles. Every option shows why it is suggested, its benefits, the risks to check with a local expert and what we do not know.

CREATIVE PARTS

We took the old idea of the farmer's almanac and rewrote it with satellite-era data. Our "bad year" test scores each rotation for the average year, the driest year and the hottest year in the record, so farmers can see which options survive a hard season. Every number is labelled as NASA data, calculated by us or a team estimate.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Farmers get a clear, comparable view of their options in minutes, without needing technical skills. We hope it helps them think about water use and soil health before choosing a rotation, while keeping the final decision with them and their local experts.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one web page that runs in a browser with no server. Leaflet for the map, Esri satellite imagery and CARTO map tiles, NASA POWER daily API for the data, Google Maps links for Street View, Visual Studio Code as our editor, and ordinary laptops. We also used an AI assistant (Claude) to help write code and text.
